claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a lower-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
The as-cast TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
A post-solidification aging treatment at about 800–900 °C can induce a uniform distribution of nanoscale precipitates in the TiVNbTa BCC matrix.
Fine nanoscale precipitates can occur within the BCC matrix of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The aging-induced precipitates in TiVNbTa will remain thermally stable at 1273 K.
The aging-induced precipitates will be Ti-rich or Ta-based.
The nanoscale precipitates will pin or impede dislocations in TiVNbTa at elevated temperature.
The precipitates will obstruct both dislocation glide and dislocation climb.
Precipitation strengthening will reduce thermally activated softening of TiVNbTa.
The aging treatment will increase the TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K relative to the 330 MPa baseline.
The aged TiVNbTa alloy may achieve a yield strength of at least approximately 500 MPa at 1273 K.
The aged TiVNbTa alloy will retain approximately 30% compressive strain capacity at 1273 K.
The applicable service condition is approximately 1273 K under compressive loading up to 30% strain between W and CuCrZr.
Thermal cycling and long-duration high-temperature exposure should be included in evaluation of the intermediate layer.
A controlled comparison of as-cast and aged TiVNbTa samples at 1273 K can test the proposed strengthening effect.
The hypothesis is falsified if aging fails to increase yield strength by at least 20% over 330 MPa without reducing ductility relative to the as-cast control.
